005package org.wpilib.util;
006
007import java.util.Objects;
008
009/**
010 * Represents colors.
011 *
012 * <p>Limited to 12 bits of precision.
013 */
014public class Color {
015  /** Red component (0-1). */
016  public final double red;
017
018  /** Green component (0-1). */
019  public final double green;
020
021  /** Blue component (0-1). */
022  public final double blue;
023
024  private String m_name;
025
026  /** Constructs a default color (black). */
027  public Color() {
028    red = 0.0;
029    green = 0.0;
030    blue = 0.0;
031  }
032
033  /**
034   * Constructs a Color from doubles.
035   *
036   * @param red Red value (0-1)
037   * @param green Green value (0-1)
038   * @param blue Blue value (0-1)
039   */
040  public Color(double red, double green, double blue) {
041    this.red = roundAndClamp(red);
042    this.green = roundAndClamp(green);
043    this.blue = roundAndClamp(blue);
044    this.m_name = null;
045  }
046
047  /**
048   * Constructs a Color from ints.
049   *
050   * @param red Red value (0-255)
051   * @param green Green value (0-255)
052   * @param blue Blue value (0-255)
053   */
054  public Color(int red, int green, int blue) {
055    this(red / 255.0, green / 255.0, blue / 255.0);
056  }
057
058  /**
059   * Constructs a Color from a Color8Bit.
060   *
061   * @param color The color
062   */
063  public Color(Color8Bit color) {
064    this(color.red / 255.0, color.green / 255.0, color.blue / 255.0);
065  }
066
067  /**
068   * Constructs a Color from doubles.
069   *
070   * @param red Red value (0-1)
071   * @param green Green value (0-1)
072   * @param blue Blue value (0-1)
073   */
074  private Color(double red, double green, double blue, String name) {
075    this.red = roundAndClamp(red);
076    this.green = roundAndClamp(green);
077    this.blue = roundAndClamp(blue);
078    this.m_name = name;
079  }
080
081  /**
082   * Makes a Color from a string.
083   *
084   * @param str a string of the format <code>#RRGGBB</code>, <code>rgb(R, G, B)</code>, or <code>
085   *     ConstantName</code>
086   * @return the Color
087   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the string is invalid.
088   */
089  public static Color fromString(String str) {
090    if (str == null || str.isBlank()) {
091      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid color string \"" + str + "\"");
092    }
093
094    // #RRGGBB style
095    if (str.charAt(0) == '#') {
096      if (str.length() != 7) {
097        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid hex string \"" + str + "\"");
098      }
099      return new Color(
100          Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1, 3), 16),
101          Integer.parseInt(str.substring(3, 5), 16),
102          Integer.parseInt(str.substring(5, 7), 16));
103    }
104
105    // RGB style
106    if (str.startsWith("rgb(") && str.endsWith(")")) {
107      String[] components = str.substring(4, str.length() - 1).split(",");
108      if (components.length != 3) {
109        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid RGB string \"" + str + "\"");
110      }
111      try {
112        return new Color(
113            Integer.parseInt(components[0].trim()),
114            Integer.parseInt(components[1].trim()),
115            Integer.parseInt(components[2].trim()));
116      } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
117        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid RGB string \"" + str + "\"");
118      }
119    }
120
121    // try to parse as a named color by matching against k-prefixed static constants in the Color
122    // class
123    for (var field : Color.class.getFields()) {
124      if (java.lang.reflect.Modifier.isStatic(field.getModifiers())
125          && Color.class.isAssignableFrom(field.getType())
126          && field.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(str)) {
127        try {
128          return (Color) field.get(null);
129        } catch (IllegalAccessException e) {
130          // Ignore and continue
131        }
132      }
133    }
134
135    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid color string \"" + str + "\"");
136  }
137
138  /**
139   * Creates a Color from HSV values.
140   *
141   * @param h The h value [0-180)
142   * @param s The s value [0-255]
143   * @param v The v value [0-255]
144   * @return The color
145   */
146  public static Color fromHSV(int h, int s, int v) {
147    int rgb = hsvToRgb(h, s, v);
148    return new Color(
149        unpackRGB(rgb, RGBChannel.RED),
150        unpackRGB(rgb, RGBChannel.GREEN),
151        unpackRGB(rgb, RGBChannel.BLUE));
152  }
153
154  @Override
155  public boolean equals(Object other) {
156    if (this == other) {
157      return true;
158    }
159    if (other == null) {
160      return false;
161    }
162
163    return other instanceof Color color
164        && Double.compare(color.red, red) == 0
165        && Double.compare(color.green, green) == 0
166        && Double.compare(color.blue, blue) == 0;
167  }
168
169  @Override
170  public int hashCode() {
171    return Objects.hash(red, green, blue);
172  }
173
174  @Override
175  public String toString() {
176    if (m_name == null) {
177      // cache hex conversion
178      m_name = toHexString();
179    }
180    return m_name;
181  }
182
183  /**
184   * Return this color represented as a hex string.
185   *
186   * @return a string of the format <code>#RRGGBB</code>
187   */
188  public String toHexString() {
189    return String.format(
190        "#%02X%02X%02X", (int) (red * 255), (int) (green * 255), (int) (blue * 255));
191  }
192
193  private static double roundAndClamp(double value) {
194    return Math.clamp(Math.ceil(value * (1 << 12)) / (1 << 12), 0.0, 1.0);
195  }
196
197  private static int lerp(int a, int b, double t) {
198    return (int) (a + (b - a) * t);
199  }
200
201  // Helper methods
202
203  /**
204   * Converts HSV values to RGB values. The returned RGB color is packed into a 32-bit integer for
205   * memory performance reasons.
206   *
207   * @param h The h value [0-180)
208   * @param s The s value [0-255]
209   * @param v The v value [0-255]
210   * @return the packed RGB color
211   */
212  public static int hsvToRgb(int h, int s, int v) {
213    // Loosely based on
214    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSL_and_HSV#HSV_to_RGB
215    // The hue range is split into 60 degree regions where in each region there
216    // is one rgb component at a low value (m), one at a high value (v) and one
217    // that changes (X) from low to high (X+m) or high to low (v-X)
218
219    // Difference between highest and lowest value of any rgb component
220    final int chroma = (s * v) / 255;
221
222    // Because hue is 0-180 rather than 0-360 use 30 not 60
223    final int region = (h / 30) % 6;
224
225    // Remainder converted from 0-30 to 0-255
226    final int remainder = (int) Math.round((h % 30) * (255 / 30.0));
227
228    // Value of the lowest rgb component
229    final int m = v - chroma;
230
231    // Goes from 0 to chroma as hue increases
232    final int X = (chroma * remainder) >> 8;
233
234    int red;
235    int green;
236    int blue;
237    switch (region) {
238      case 0:
239        red = v;
240        green = X + m;
241        blue = m;
242        break;
243      case 1:
244        red = v - X;
245        green = v;
246        blue = m;
247        break;
248      case 2:
249        red = m;
250        green = v;
251        blue = X + m;
252        break;
253      case 3:
254        red = m;
255        green = v - X;
256        blue = v;
257        break;
258      case 4:
259        red = X + m;
260        green = m;
261        blue = v;
262        break;
263      default:
264        red = v;
265        green = m;
266        blue = v - X;
267        break;
268    }
269    return packRGB(red, green, blue);
270  }
271
272  /** Represents a color channel in an RGB color. */
273  public enum RGBChannel {
274    /** The red channel of an RGB color. */
275    RED,
276    /** The green channel of an RGB color. */
277    GREEN,
278    /** The blue channel of an RGB color. */
279    BLUE
280  }
281
282  /**
283   * Packs 3 RGB values into a single 32-bit integer. These values can be unpacked with {@link
284   * #unpackRGB(int, RGBChannel)} to retrieve the values. This is helpful for avoiding memory
285   * allocations of new {@code Color} objects and its resulting garbage collector pressure.
286   *
287   * @param r the value of the first channel to pack
288   * @param g the value of the second channel to pack
289   * @param b the value of the third channel to pack
290   * @return the packed integer
291   */
292  public static int packRGB(int r, int g, int b) {
293    return (r & 0xFF) << 16 | (g & 0xFF) << 8 | (b & 0xFF);
294  }
295
296  /**
297   * Unpacks a single color channel from a packed 32-bit RGB integer.
298   *
299   * <p>Note: Packed RGB colors are expected to be in byte order [empty][red][green][blue].
300   *
301   * @param packedColor the packed color to extract from
302   * @param channel the color channel to unpack
303   * @return the value of the stored color channel
304   */
305  public static int unpackRGB(int packedColor, RGBChannel channel) {
306    return switch (channel) {
307      case RED -> (packedColor >> 16) & 0xFF;
308      case GREEN -> (packedColor >> 8) & 0xFF;
309      case BLUE -> packedColor & 0xFF;
310    };
311  }
312
313  /**
314   * Performs a linear interpolation between two colors in the RGB colorspace.
315   *
316   * @param a the first color to interpolate from
317   * @param b the second color to interpolate from
318   * @param t the interpolation scale in [0, 1]
319   * @return the interpolated color
320   */
321  public static Color lerpRGB(Color a, Color b, double t) {
322    int packedRGB = lerpRGB(a.red, a.green, a.blue, b.red, b.green, b.blue, t);
323
324    return new Color(
325        unpackRGB(packedRGB, RGBChannel.RED),
326        unpackRGB(packedRGB, RGBChannel.GREEN),
327        unpackRGB(packedRGB, RGBChannel.BLUE));
328  }
329
330  /**
331   * Linearly interpolates between two RGB colors represented by the (r1, g1, b1) and (r2, g2, b2)
332   * triplets. For memory performance reasons, the output color is returned packed into a single
333   * 32-bit integer; use {@link #unpackRGB(int, RGBChannel)} to extract the values for the
334   * individual red, green, and blue channels.
335   *
336   * @param r1 the red value of the first color, in [0, 1]
337   * @param g1 the green value of the first color, in [0, 1]
338   * @param b1 the blue value of the first color, in [0, 1]
339   * @param r2 the red value of the second color, in [0, 1]
340   * @param g2 the green value of the second color, in [0, 1]
341   * @param b2 the blue value of the second color, in [0, 1]
342   * @param t the interpolation value, in [0, 1]
343   * @return the interpolated color, packed in a 32-bit integer
344   */
345  public static int lerpRGB(
346      double r1, double g1, double b1, double r2, double g2, double b2, double t) {
347    return lerpRGB(
348        (int) (r1 * 255),
349        (int) (g1 * 255),
350        (int) (b1 * 255),
351        (int) (r2 * 255),
352        (int) (g2 * 255),
353        (int) (b2 * 255),
354        t);
355  }
356
357  /**
358   * Linearly interpolates between two RGB colors represented by the (r1, g1, b1) and (r2, g2, b2)
359   * triplets. For memory performance reasons, the output color is returned packed into a single
360   * 32-bit integer; use {@link #unpackRGB(int, RGBChannel)} to extract the values for the
361   * individual red, green, and blue channels.
362   *
363   * @param r1 the red value of the first color, in [0, 255]
364   * @param g1 the green value of the first color, in [0, 255]
365   * @param b1 the blue value of the first color, in [0, 255]
366   * @param r2 the red value of the second color, in [0, 255]
367   * @param g2 the green value of the second color, in [0, 255]
368   * @param b2 the blue value of the second color, in [0, 255]
369   * @param t the interpolation value, in [0, 1]
370   * @return the interpolated color, packed in a 32-bit integer
371   */
372  public static int lerpRGB(int r1, int g1, int b1, int r2, int g2, int b2, double t) {
373    return packRGB(lerp(r1, r2, t), lerp(g1, g2, t), lerp(b1, b2, t));
374  }
